canonical_name: Thompson transfer lemma (1968 Lemma 5.38(a)(i) source candidate; identity review open)
literal_source_claim_zh: 关于群局部性质与整体性质的关系
literal_source_claim_en: About the relation between local and global properties of groups.
source_attribution: John Thompson, 1964 (catalog metadata only; conflicts with the located 1968 primary source)
source_candidate_statement_not_yet_canon: Let G be a finite group of even order with no subgroup of index two. If S is a Sylow 2-subgroup of G and M is a maximal subgroup of S, then every involution of S has a G-conjugate in M.
source_candidate_locator: John G. Thompson, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 74 (1968), Lemma 5.38(a)(i), printed page 411, DOI 10.1090/S0002-9904-1968-11953-6
statement_blocker: The catalog gives no formula or citation and dates the result to 1964. A precise primary clause was located in Thompson 1968 through Lynd's eponym crosswalk, but an independent reviewer has not accepted that identity, the full Lemma 5.38 versus part (a)(i) boundary, or the relationship between Thompson's universal involution clause and Lynd's restricted u outside M form. Choosing one as canonical now would overstate the intake evidence.
domain_and_universes: Prospective source scope: a finite group G; its natural cardinality and subgroup indices; a Sylow 2-subgroup S represented as a nested carrier; a maximal proper subgroup M of S; an involution u in S; and ambient-G conjugacy. Exact universe and typeclass binders remain for the statement phase.
conclusion: Prospective source conclusion only: every source-defined involution in S has an ambient-G conjugate whose nested subgroup carrier lies in M. Exact witness and coercion encoding remain open.
